Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject a `<script>` right after `<head>` that polls for `window.__jusprinBridge`, wraps its `deliver` to `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/log?'+JSON)` the envelopes of interest, and sends page messages with `window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge',version:1,id,type,payload}))`.
2. Serve the dir with `python3 -m http.server <port> --bind 127.0.0.1 > server.log`; the request log is the test output.
3. Launch the built binary directly: `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/page.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with real *_api_key items deleted and TESTONLY keys added>`. """Serves the instrumented Agent page, records what the host sends it, and
hands each page the messages queued for it."""
import json, sys, threading
from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs

queues, lock = {}, threading.Lock()
log = open('log.jsonl', 'a', buffering=1)

class Handler(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *args): pass
    def _json(self, value):
        body = json.dumps(value).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
        self.send_header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*')
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    def do_GET(self):
        url = urlparse(self.path)
        q = parse_qs(url.query)
        if url.path == '/cmd':
            panel = q.get('panel', [''])[0]
            with lock:
                items = queues.pop(panel, [])
            return self._json(items)
        return super().do_GET()
    def end_headers(self):
        # The app's web views must load this run's page, never a cached one.
        self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')
        super().end_headers()
    def do_POST(self):
        url = urlparse(self.path)
        q = parse_qs(url.query)
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0)) or 0)
        if url.path == '/log':
            log.write(body.decode() + '\n')
            return self._json({})
        if url.path == '/queue':
            panel = q.get('panel', [''])[0]
            with lock:
                queues.setdefault(panel, []).extend(json.loads(body))
            return self._json({})
        self.send_response(404); self.end_headers()
    def do_OPTIONS(self):
        self.send_response(204)
        self.send_header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*')
        self.send_header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', '*')
        self.send_header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'GET, POST')
        self.end_headers()

ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()

content.text:
I ran the live test against staging, and everything I could drive passed. Google sign-in is the one path I couldn't finish. I used a copy of the first-run build on a new, empty data folder, and pressed its buttons through a logging script injected into its pages, without screen control.

**Results:**
- **Email code sign-in passes.** I entered a new address, `k+stg-e2e1@obico.io`, and asked for a code. Staging emailed it within seconds, and I read it from your inbox.
  - A wrong code kept the app on the code step with the "wrong code" message.
  - The real code signed the app in. Staging made the account, the welcome card showed it with 500 credits, and the app moved on to the Printers step.
  - The app saved the JusPrin provider, the token, the account's email and both models.
- **A wrong password is refused.** Using the same address from a second empty data folder, the app stayed on the email step showing "wrong password".
- **Chat works on both models.** I skipped to a default printer, reached Home and sent the same question to each model: "Which printer and layer height is this project set to?"
  - Expert read the setting with a tool and answered correctly. The balance went from 500 to 495 credits.
  - Standard, in a new chat, answered correctly too. The balance went to 494.
- **Google sign-in:** I didn't get past the browser. The app opened your browser to staging's sign-in page and waited. The browser it opened wasn't signed in to staging, so the page asked for a login, and I can't sign in to Google for you. I cancelled the sign-in in the app. Earlier your own attempt got through the browser step and failed only when the app read the model list. Email sign-in now gets through that same model-list check.

**Two things for you:**
- A staging sign-in tab is open in your browser from the Google test. You can close it, or sign in there to finish the Google test.
- The Standard chat's title stayed "New chat", while the Expert chat got a real title. I closed the app a few seconds after the reply, so the title request may still have been running. I haven't checked further. It could also be the known problem where Standard answers the title request instead of writing a title.

The test used two chat messages. The test account remains on staging with 494 credits. I closed the test app and its log servers.

input.ask: Should accounts made by JusPrin sign-in skip the Obico trial and welcome email?

content.text:
I checked the last two hours of k@obico.io with gog. There's one finding from the staging test.

**The new JusPrin test account got Obico's welcome email.** Four and a half minutes after `k+stg-e2e1@obico.io` signed in to JusPrin for the first time, staging sent it "Get started with Obico", from Obi The Owl. The email introduces Obico's AI print-failure detection and says the person has 30 days of free access to every AI Premium feature. So a JusPrin user's first email after the sign-in code is about a different product.

**Why it happens:** tsd-enterprise creates an Obico subscription for every new account, and this isn't specific to JusPrin.
- `start_free_trial` in `web_ent/app_ent/models.py` runs whenever an account is created, whatever created it.
- It gives the account a 30-day Obico "pro-trial" subscription.
- Five minutes later it schedules `setup_free_trial` (`web_ent/app_ent/tasks/base_tasks.py`), which credits 250 detective hours and sends "Get started with Obico".
- Only accounts outside the base syndicate are skipped, and JusPrin accounts are in the base syndicate.

So every JusPrin sign-up gets the Obico trial and the email: the new email-code path, the Google path (which makes the account through the website's sign-up), and any other path.

**Decision needed:** should accounts made by JusPrin sign-in skip the Obico trial and the "Get started with Obico" email?
- **Skip both (my pick).** A JusPrin user wouldn't get a second product's trial and marketing as their first email. The email-code path makes its own accounts, so marking those is straightforward. The Google path makes accounts through the website's sign-up, so it would need a way to recognise that the sign-up came from the JusPrin app's sign-in, which is more work. It also changes who counts as an Obico trial user.
- **Leave as is.** No work, and every JusPrin user also gets an Obico trial. The cost is the confusing first email, and Obico trial numbers that include people who came for JusPrin.

The rest of the last two hours is unrelated to this work, and I haven't touched any of it:
- Joe Macina asked to stop account notifications.
- Dalibor Stepek asked for his account to be deleted.
- Chargebee reported a webhook failure.
- Obico Admin sent a "subscription has expired" notice.
- A Sentry reply arrived.
Skip both

Test email, Google and website sign-up paths
Commit, release to staging, verify live

def skip_obico_trial(sender, request, user, sociallogin=None, **kwargs):
    """allauth's user_signed_up: an account made by signing in to JusPrin 2
    starts on Obico's free plan. Every new account otherwise gets Obico's
    30-day AI Premium trial (app_ent.models.start_free_trial) and, five minutes
    later, its credit and the "Get started with Obico" email (setup_free_trial,
    which skips an account no longer in the trial). The trial is ended rather
    than deleted because nearly every account has a Subscription and code
    across app_ent reads it; plan_id 'free' keeps the daily expiry task from
    sending "Your free Obico trial just ended"."""
    if not _signs_in_to_jusprin(request, sociallogin):
        return
    sub = Subscription.objects.get(user=user, plan_id='pro-trial')
    sub.plan_id = 'free'
    sub.expired_at = timezone.now()
    sub.save()
    sub.update_pro_status_on_user()


def _signs_in_to_jusprin(request, sociallogin) -> bool:
    """The app's own email sign-in, or a website or Google sign-up on the way
    to authorizing the JusPrin 2 application (the page the app opened)."""
    match = request.resolver_match
    if match is not None and match.url_name == 'jusprin_v2_auth_code_request':
        return True
    next_url = (sociallogin.state.get('next') if sociallogin else None) or request.POST.get('next') or request.GET.get('next')
    url = urlparse(next_url or '')
    return (url.path == reverse('oauth2_provider:authorize')
            and parse_qs(url.query).get('client_id') == [settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID])

input.recap: Accounts made by signing in to JusPrin 2 now start on Obico's free plan, with no trial and no "Get started with Obico" email. Verified on staging (obi.4063) with a new email sign-in. Production is unchanged, and the Google path is covered by tests only.

content.text:
Done: accounts made by signing in to JusPrin 2 now skip both Obico's trial and its "Get started with Obico" email. The change is commit 5daee67e1b on tsd-enterprise master. It's live on staging as image obi.4063; production is unchanged.

**How it works:** when allauth reports a new account, the server checks whether it came from a JusPrin 2 sign-in. That covers three cases:
- the app's own email sign-in;
- a website sign-up made on the way to the JusPrin 2 authorization page the app opened;
- a Google sign-up made on the way to that same page.

If so, it ends the Obico trial on the spot. The job that runs five minutes later then finds no trial, so it grants no detective hours and sends no welcome email. The account keeps its subscription record as plan "free", ended at sign-up. I chose that over deleting the record because all but 15 of production's 251,000 accounts have one, and the server reads it in many places. The "free" plan name also keeps the daily job from sending "Your free Obico trial just ended". Sign-ups for anything else keep the trial as before, including sign-ups through JusPrin v1's app.

**Tests:**
- Before the fix, three new tests showed the trial being granted for each of the three JusPrin paths. They pass after the fix.
- Two control tests confirm a plain website sign-up and a sign-up for JusPrin v1's app still get the trial.
- All other server tests pass: 286, plus the 34 Google sign-in tests.
- On staging, the login page's Google button carries the JusPrin authorization address along, which is what the Google case relies on.

**Live check on staging:** I signed in a new address, `k+stg-e2e2@obico.io`, by email code through the same server calls the app makes.
- It has plan "free", no trial, no hour credit, and isn't marked as an Obico paying user.
- The account from the earlier test, made before the fix, still has the trial.
- Seven minutes later its only email was the sign-in code. The five-minute job ran and finished without sending anything.

**Not covered:**
- I couldn't run a real Google sign-up, because that needs a Google account. The tests and the staging link check cover it.
- `k+stg-e2e1@obico.io` still has the Obico trial, since I didn't change accounts made before the fix.
- The ops change is commit 564b789, local only. The ops repo is now three commits ahead of its remote.
what did you do to disable the emails?

I didn't switch off any email directly. I took away the trial that the welcome email depends on, so the existing code skips the email by its own rules.

Here's the sequence for a new account.

**Before the fix:**
1. The account is created. `start_free_trial` (in `web_ent/app_ent/models.py`) runs on every new account. It gives the account a subscription with plan `pro-trial` that ends in 30 days, and schedules `setup_free_trial` to run five minutes later.
2. Five minutes later, `setup_free_trial` (in `web_ent/app_ent/tasks/base_tasks.py`) checks whether the account is still in the trial. It is, so it credits 250 detective hours and sends "Get started with Obico".

**After the fix:** step 1 is unchanged. Right after it, still in the same request, allauth fires its "a new account signed up" signal. I added a listener on that signal, `skip_obico_trial` in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py`, connected in `web_ent/jusprin/apps.py`. When the sign-up came from JusPrin 2, it changes the new subscription's plan from `pro-trial` to `free` and sets its end date to now. Five minutes later, `setup_free_trial` sees the account isn't in the trial and returns immediately. That check was already there for people who skip the trial by buying a kit. So no hours are credited and no email goes out.

The plan name matters for a second email. A daily job, `expire_plans`, sends "Your free Obico trial just ended" to any `pro-trial` subscription that ended in the last three days. If I had only ended the trial and left the plan as `pro-trial`, the account would have got that email within a day. Plan `free` isn't `pro-trial`, so that job leaves it alone. The "5 days left on your Obico free trial" reminder only looks at `pro-trial` too.

I changed nothing in the email code or the trial code.

Revert your change. create a new task chip to look at if we can leverage the concept of syndicate to streamline this process. This feature is very close to what syndicate was designed for: branding, cutomized trickle emails, etc. 

The only challenge I can see is to let the user use the same account for both obico and jusprin. Investigate if there is an elegant solution to let two syndicates share the same allauth account

2	
3	Written 2026-11-03. Read from tsd-enterprise master (cf01e7adbf) and obico-server 731f6947 (allauth 65.21.1). Nothing was changed in any repo or on staging.
4	
5	## What the code does today
6	
7	A syndicate today does two jobs, both stored in `User.syndicate`.
8	
9	It is the account pool. `User` is unique on (email, syndicate), usernames are `{email}_{syndicate.id}`, and every lookup by address stays inside the request's syndicate: password login (`SyndicateSpecificBackend`), password reset, add-email, Google sign-in (`SocialAccountAdapter.pre_social_login`) and JusPrin's email-code sign-in (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py`).
10	
11	It is also the brand: display name and logo (`SYNDICATES` in settings), the from-address of allauth and notification emails, the email layout under `templates/<syndicate>/email/`, the domain in links, and which drip emails run. Every Obico trial and onboarding email filters on `syndicate__name='base'`. Kingroon has one drip of its own.
12	
13	`syndicate_from_request` checks the signed-in user's syndicate first, then the `X-Obico-Syndicate` header, then the domain. Kingroon and Yumi have their own domains.
14	
15	A `jusprin` entry already exists in `SYNDICATES`, but there is no database row for it. JusPrin v1 pages get JusPrin branding from a User-Agent check in `app/context_processors.py`, marked "TODO: JusPrin syndicate hack". So today every JusPrin v1 account is a base-syndicate Obico account.
16	
17	Three more facts matter for the options:
18	- The Obico subscription, `JusPrinPlan` and the JusPrin credit ledger are separate tables keyed on the user, so one user can already hold both products' billing.
19	- Every new user gets a 30-day `pro-trial` subscription row from a post-save signal, whatever the syndicate. Only the trial credits, the welcome email and the drips skip accounts outside base.
20	- Google IDs are stored as `{google id}_{site id}`, so a Google sign-in is tied to the domain, not to the syndicate.
21	
22	allauth 65 has no accounts per tenant. Its docs mention sites only for social apps (provider credentials per domain). Products that share one account across tenants, such as ABP's "shared user accounts" and django-tenant-users, use one global user with a membership per tenant, and the email is unique everywhere.
23	
24	## Options
25	
26	1. **A classic syndicate.** This is cheap: a database row, a domain, templates. But anyone who already has Obico gets a second, empty account when they sign in to JusPrin. Existing JusPrin v1 users, some of them paying, would also land in new accounts unless their data is moved. It fails the one-account goal.
27	2. **One user with a set of syndicates.** Kingroon and Yumi would start sharing accounts too. About 160 lines that read `user.syndicate` would have to learn which syndicate a request is for. And accounts that share an email across syndicates would have to be merged first. I have not counted those accounts. This is the largest option.
28	3. **Linked accounts.** allauth keeps the password, email addresses and Google links on each user row, so linked rows would need constant syncing. I'd rule this out.
29	4. **Separate the account pool from the brand (proposal, my pick).** JusPrin becomes a syndicate for branding: its own row, logo, from-address, email templates and drips. Its accounts stay in the base pool, so an Obico account signs in to JusPrin unchanged, with the same password and Google link. The new code is a per-request brand lookup and a per-user record of which brands the person uses:
30	   - The brand lookup reads JusPrin's OAuth applications, the `/jusprin/v2/` paths and any future JusPrin domain. It replaces the User-Agent check.
31	   - Drips filter on the brand record instead of `syndicate__name`, and existing JusPrin v1 users need only a backfill of that record.
32	   - Usernames, the login backend and Google sign-in stay as they are.
33	   - The cost is the brand lookup, one table with its migration, and moving the trial check from "the account's syndicate is base" to "the account was created through the Obico brand". JusPrin's own drips have to be written under any option.
34	
35	## Decisions
36	
37	Decision needed: should JusPrin be a brand-only syndicate whose accounts live in the base pool (option 4), or a full syndicate with its own accounts (option 1)? Option 4 keeps one account per person and costs a brand lookup, one table and a backfill. Option 1 is mostly configuration, but it gives Obico users and existing JusPrin v1 users a second, empty account. This is your call because it sets what a syndicate means. I recommend option 4.
38	
39	Decision needed: when someone who signed up through JusPrin later signs in to the Obico website, should they get Obico's 30-day AI Premium trial and welcome email then, or never? Giving it on their first Obico sign-in treats them like any new Obico user and needs a trigger on that sign-in. Never giving it is simpler but leaves them on the free plan with no onboarding. This is a product choice about the trial. I lean toward giving it on the first Obico sign-in.

===== assistant 2026-11-02T06:31:00.566Z
Serve them from the server. Your two reasons are the right ones, and there is a third: a pricing page is marketing copy, and marketing copy changes on a different cadence from a C++ release. Steam is the clearest precedent, its store and account pages are web content inside the native client for exactly this reason, while the library and downloads stay native.

The one place it does not work is the composer. The balance ring, the hover panel, the tier prices in the picker, and the pre-send "Send with Basic" check all render inside a native-feeling panel on every keystroke and must degrade gracefully when the network is down. Those need a small API, and the plan already has it: the `/account` endpoint for the balance and lots, and the per-alias `credits` field on `/models` for the prices. So the split is: the composer learns numbers from the API, and everything a person reads at leisure (Account, usage history, plans, the Obico price) is a page the server owns. Version skew then shrinks to that one API, which is cheap to keep backward compatible because it only returns numbers.

The downsides of the webview route, with what I would do about each:

- **Signing the webview in.** The app holds an OAuth bearer token; a served page needs a session cookie. The token must not go in the page URL, since URLs end up in logs. The clean pattern is one gateway call that trades the bearer token for a short-lived, single-use login URL; the webview opens it, the server sets the cookie and redirects to the page. That endpoint does not exist yet and is the real cost of this approach, about a day.
- **Offline.** The Account page is blank without a network. Acceptable, as long as the composer still shows the last known balance from the API and the page shows a plain "can't reach JusPrin" state instead of a browser error.
- **Theme.** The page must follow the app's light or dark setting and the design tokens. Pass the theme in the URL and have the page use the same token CSS the Agent page uses, otherwise it is a second design system to keep in sync.
- **Checkout.** Keep the actual Chargebee checkout in the system browser, as the plan already says. My expectation, not verified, is that card verification flows (3-D Secure redirects) are the thing most likely to break inside an embedded webview. The served pricing page then just hands off to the browser and the app refreshes the balance on focus.
- **Bridge contract.** The page will want to tell the app two things, "balance changed" and "close me". Keep that to a tiny message set that never changes, so a three-year-old app still works with today's page.
- **Latency.** A remote page takes a visible moment to appear when Preferences › Account opens. Fine there, which is another reason it must never be the composer.

One consequence for the design just drawn: boards 4a to 4c (Account) and 5a and 5b (pricing) become one web page the server renders, not AgentUI panels, so their implementation moves from the client repo to tsd-enterprise. The boards themselves do not change.

You did discuss it, but for the Account and pricing pages, not the first-run screens. I found no record of you deciding it. Every later plan I checked still lists it as open.

**Where it was:** a pricing brainstorm session on November 2. You asked whether the Account and subscription pages should load from the server into a webview inside the app, rather than the app building them from API data.

**Your reasons for serving them from the server:**
- Pricing will need a lot of experimenting, and server pages can change without an app release.
- Old app versions can't get in the way of the latest pricing.

**The session's answer** was to serve them from the server. It added that pricing copy changes more often than the app is released, and gave Steam's store pages inside its client as the precedent. It kept one exception: the credit indicators in the chat composer (the balance ring, the tier prices in the model picker, the check before sending) stay in the app. They get their numbers from a small API, because they redraw constantly and have to keep working offline.

**The downsides it listed:**
- **Signing the webview in.** The app holds a token, but a web page needs a session cookie. That needs a new gateway call that trades the token for a single-use login link, estimated at about a day of work.
- **Offline.** The Account page goes blank without a network, so it needs a plain "can't reach JusPrin" state.
- **Theme.** The page must follow the app's light or dark mode and use the same design tokens.
- **Checkout.** Chargebee checkout stays in the system browser. The session expected card verification to break inside an embedded webview, but hadn't verified that.
- **Messages to the app.** The page tells the app only "balance changed" and "close me", and those two messages must never change.
- **Load time.** There's a short delay when the page opens.

**Status:** the briefs written later that day call it "Kenneth's decision 12", still open. The Account, pricing and Chargebee work was held back waiting for it, along with the domain decision. The domain is now settled as jusprinv2.obico.io. I found nothing showing you made the webview call.

Yes. For "Continue with Google" to go straight to Google, the server needs almost nothing new. The change is in the app: it should open a different address.

**What I checked**

- The server already starts Google sign-in from a plain link. `SOCIALACCOUNT_LOGIN_ON_GET = True` is set in obico-server's settings, so opening the sign-in address skips our sign-in page.
- I tested this on staging. Opening `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io/accounts/google/login/?process=login&next=<the app's /o/authorize/ address>` goes straight to Google, with JusPrin 2's own return address. app-stg.obico.io behaves the same way.
- On staging the JusPrin2 app is set to skip the "Authorize this app?" page (`skip_authorization` is true). So after Google, the person goes straight back to the app.
- The "You're signed in, go back to JusPrin" page already exists on the server. The app sends the browser there after it finishes, and a "didn't finish" page exists too.

**What needs to change**

1. **In the app:** when the person clicks Continue with Google, open the Google sign-in address above with the current authorize address as `next`, instead of opening `/o/authorize/` directly. It's a small change in `CloudAccount.cpp`.
2. **On the server, nothing is required.** Expected route after the app change: Google, then `/o/authorize/`, then back to the app, then the "signed in" page. Google's own return address should keep `next`. My earlier work found that's how allauth's Google login keeps it, but I haven't watched it happen end to end.

**Still open, not verified**

- **A full Google sign-in.** It needs a real Google account in a browser, so you'd have to click through it once.
- **Cancelling at Google.** The person lands on allauth's "login cancelled" page. It's Obico's page in JusPrin colors, and it has no way back to the app. The app keeps waiting, and the email-code option on the waiting screen still works. It's probably fine for now.
- **My local server** has `skip_authorization` off, so locally you'd still see the "Authorize" page. Staging has it on.
- **Production:** the app record, Site, Google settings and DNS for jusprinv2.obico.io don't exist yet. That's rollout work.

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`

content.text:
That squash has already happened. At 12:24 today another session squashed the branch into one commit, f46e5ac05f "JusPrin Cloud account: credits, the first launch, and sign-in by email and Google at jusprinv2.obico.io", and pushed it to `origin/jusprin-newui`. So the real question is whether to keep doing it this way.

**My view: squashing works, but a merge commit gives you the same clean log for a lower cost.** The log stays clean either way. Here's what squashing costs you that a merge doesn't:

- **You lose the step history.** The one commit covers 117 files and replaces 19 commits, each with its own message. When `git blame` points at a line in that commit, you can't tell which step added it or why. `git bisect` can only narrow a bug down to the whole feature. The step-by-step commits now live only on the unpushed local branch `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741`.
- **Git no longer knows which branches are merged.** The branch had already taken in the credits branch. As a result, `origin/credits-integration-2026-11` now shows 16 commits git counts as unmerged, even though all of their content is in f46e5ac05f. Anyone who later merges or rebases that branch gets those commits replayed, with conflicts. `claude/credits-onboarding` shows 3 commits the same way.

**The alternative** is to merge with `--no-ff`, write a one-line summary as the merge message, and read the log with `git log --first-parent`. That view shows one line per feature, just like the squash, and the step commits are still underneath for blame and bisect. jusprin-newui already does this for some branches, for example "Merge claude/tool-results-truth: …". Other branches were squashed, so right now the history uses both styles.

**For this commit, I'd leave it as it is.** Undoing a squash that's already pushed means rewriting the shared jusprin-newui branch, and that's worse than anything above. Two small things would cover what it lost:

1. Push `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741` to GitHub, so the step history is kept somewhere besides this Mac.
2. Delete `credits-integration-2026-11` and `claude/credits-onboarding`, or label them as already merged, so nobody merges them a second time.

Decision needed: from now on, should feature branches land on jusprin-newui as a squash or as a `--no-ff` merge? Squashing keeps the full `git log` short, but it gives up the step history and leaves the merged branches looking unmerged. A `--no-ff` merge keeps both and looks the same when you read the log with `--first-parent`. This one is yours because it sets how every session lands its work. I'd pick `--no-ff` merges. Which do you want?
Okay, go with what you suggested.
